observation: Lint-gate blind spot for consistency work: npm run lint only flags arbitrary-value Tailwind classes (gap-[16px], text-[14px]), NOT alias classes (gap-4, text-sm) which are the actual divergences a consistency pass targets. AC-1/AC-2 had no enforcing gate until a custom enumerated static check (scripts/ag7-no-divergent-classes.ts) was added. Caught by Phase-2 critique pre-build. Candidate: any consistency/token-adoption WP must ship its own enumerated static check; lint alone is false coverage.

TDD applied to a presentation/consistency pass: the static check was written red (84 violations on current code) then driven to 0 as 10 sections converted. Makes a presentation pass falsifiable; gate has enumeration guard (10 files, non-empty forbidden list, whole-token bounding so gap-[12px] is not a false positive). Worth protecting as the pattern for consistency contracts.

Combined-gate blind spot (W2): ml-2 (8px off-grid) slipped BOTH gates — the AG7 check forbade gap-*/text-* but not margin aliases; eslint forbade arbitrary m-[Npx] but not aliases. Each gate reasonable alone; the union left a hole found only at code review. Cheap fix (extend check with ml/mr/mt/mb-* aliases). Candidate: a custom static gate should document its blacklist scope + cross-gate dependency so omissions read as intentional vs gap.

M-presentation WP cost profile: low. AG7 (M, 27 files +1028/-587, 10 settings sections) ran all 6 phases + ship; critique APPROVED first pass (8/10,7/10) with 2 CRITICAL build-time corrections folded via 1 revision commit; review DONE 0-critical with 2 cheap WARNINGs folded; 0 builder rework loops, green phase in ONE session, 0 snapshot re-bless. Critique caught 2 real issues that would otherwise ship; review caught 2 more. Profile resembles L-process, distinct from full-stack L/M.
